name: Padmasambhava Mahavihara Monastery
description: Padmasambhava Mahavihara is a large Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Chandragiri, Gajapati district, inaugurated by the 14th Dalai Lama in 2010. It is widely regarded as the largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery in eastern India. The five-storey complex is built in traditional Himalayan architectural style and serves as a monastery-college for monks from the Tibetan refugee settlement of Phuntsokling, established after the 1959 Chinese invasion of Tibet.
coordinate_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (verified: Padmasambhava Mahavihara, Gajapati, Odisha)
notes: Coordinates confirmed via Wikipedia infobox (19.2733N, 84.2633E) and OSM Nominatim (19.2716, 84.2638). Wikimedia image confirmed: Chandragiri_Lobersing_Ganjam_Odisha1.jpg (2048x1152, CC BY-SA 3.0 by Anant Panda, Category:Padmasambhava Mahavihara). The Tibetan settlement at Chandragiri is a notable community of Tibetan refugees; description uses respectful, factual language about their history.

name: Tampara Lake
description: Tampara is a shallow coastal saltwater lake and eco-tourism destination near Chhatrapur in Ganjam district, separated from the Bay of Bengal by a narrow sand bar. Spread over approximately 320 hectares, the lake is a significant wetland habitat for migratory waterfowl and resident species. OTDC operates a tourist cottage and boating facility at the lake.
coordinate_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim verified: Tampara Lake, Chhatrapur, Ganjam, Odisha
notes: Coordinates verified via OSM Nominatim (19.347752, 84.9975178). Two Wikimedia images confirmed: Tampara_lake,_chatrapur.jpg (1900x1069) and Tampara_lake.jpg (2112x1188), both CC BY-SA 4.0. Coastal lagoon, not same location as Gopalpur-on-Sea — no production duplicate.

name: Potagarh Fort
description: Potagarh Fort is a ruined 17th-century coastal fort near Ganjam town, originally built by the Dutch and later occupied by the British East India Company. The fort stands near the mouth of the Rushikulya river and is associated with the early European trading history of the Odisha coast. It is listed as a heritage site by the Odisha State Archaeology Department.
coordinate_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim verified: Potagarh road, Ganjam, Odisha

name: Aryapalli Beach
description: Aryapalli Beach is a pristine, largely undeveloped shoreline near Chhatrapur in Ganjam district. Located adjacent to the Tampara Lake eco-zone, the beach is known for nesting of Olive Ridley sea turtles during the winter season and is included in the Rushikulya sea turtle conservation stretch. The Odisha Forest Department monitors turtle nesting activity at this beach.

name: Brundaban Palace, Paralakhemundi
description: Brundaban Palace is the ancestral seat of the Maharaja of Parlakhemundi (Gajapati rulers), located in Paralakhemundi town, Gajapati district. The palace complex, built in the 19th century, reflects the princely architectural tradition of coastal Odisha. The town of Paralakhemundi, associated with nationalist leader Gopabandhu Das, is the administrative headquarters of Gajapati district.

Wikipedia article on Paralakhemundi references the palace but does not carry a usable Commons image of the palace itself. Retained for research; needs coordinate and image verification.

name: Purunakatak Maa Bhairabi Temple
description: Purunakatak Maa Bhairabi Temple is an ancient Shakti pitha located at Purunakatak in Boudh district, on the banks of the Mahanadi River. The presiding deity is Goddess Bhairabi, worshipped as a powerful form of the divine feminine. The temple is a significant pilgrimage site for communities across Boudh district and surrounding areas.

name: Sabara Srikhetra, Koraput
description: Sabara Srikhetra is a revered pilgrimage complex in Koraput district, regarded as the sacred land of the Sabar (Sabara) community — a tribal community historically associated with the origins of the Jagannath tradition at Puri. The site celebrates the connection between Jagannath worship and indigenous Sabar cultural heritage, and is a significant destination for pilgrims from across the region.

name: Putsil Valley, Koraput
description: Putsil is a scenic highland valley in Pottangi block of Koraput district, situated in the Eastern Ghats at around 900 metres elevation. The valley is known for its dense forests, rich biodiversity including endemic butterfly species, and views across the highland ranges. It is an emerging eco-tourism site accessible from the Jeypore-Pottangi road.

name: Maliguda, Koraput
description: Maliguda is a picturesque gorge and railway tunnel site in Koraput district, situated on the Jagdalpur railway line. The narrow gorge through the Eastern Ghats, combined with a historic railway engineering marvel, makes it a notable scenic destination. The surrounding landscape of densely forested hills and the Machkund River valley is considered one of the most dramatic in southern Odisha.

name: Rani Duduma Waterfall
description: Rani Duduma is a powerful waterfall on the Machkund River in Nandapur block of Koraput district, located near the Odisha-Andhra Pradesh border. It drops from the edge of the Eastern Ghats plateau into the river gorge below. The waterfall is associated with the Machkund hydroelectric project and is accessible via the Jeypore-Nandapur road.

name: Gurupriya Bridge, Malkangiri
description: Gurupriya Bridge is a strategically and historically significant floating pontoon bridge over the Gurupriya River in Malkangiri district, constructed to connect isolated communities on the Chitrakonda peninsula. For decades it provided the only road link to areas cut off by the Balimela reservoir backwaters. The bridge and surrounding landscape of the reservoir peninsula have become an important local attraction in one of Odisha's most remote districts.

name: Manyamkonda Temple, Motu
description: Manyamkonda is a hilltop temple site in Motu block of Malkangiri district, near the Andhra Pradesh border. The site, situated in the forested terrain of the Eastern Ghats foothills, is a local pilgrimage destination for communities from both Malkangiri district and neighbouring Andhra Pradesh.

name: Indravati Dam, Thuamul Rampur
description: Indravati Dam at Thuamul Rampur in Kalahandi district is a major irrigation and hydroelectric dam across the Indravati River. The reservoir created by the dam is vast, submerging large forest areas and forming a scenic lake landscape amid the Eastern Ghats. The dam and surrounding reservoir area are accessible via Bhawanipatna and offer striking views of the highland reservoir environment.

name: Putudi Waterfall
description: Putudi Waterfall is a scenic waterfall near Phulbani in Kandhamal district, surrounded by forested hills in the Eastern Ghats. The waterfall is a popular picnic and nature tourism site for visitors to Phulbani, the district headquarters of Kandhamal. Kandhamal district, known for its coffee and spice cultivation and the hill station of Daringbadi, also includes this lesser-known natural attraction.

name: Minajhola, Rayagada
description: Minajhola is a natural waterfall and small eco-tourism site in Rayagada district, located in the Eastern Ghats landscape near Kashipur. The site is set amid forested highlands and is a local attraction in a district that is underrepresented in Odisha tourism databases. Rayagada district is in the tribal highlands region of southern Odisha, and its landscape is characterised by the Eastern Ghats terrain.
